subsystems.name: Landing and parking deck
subsystems.role: the physical pad where aircraft touch down, park and recharge.
parts: elevated steel or concrete deck sized to the rotor diameter

subsystems.name: Charging and ground power
subsystems.role: recharges aircraft batteries in minutes between flights.

subsystems.name: Navigation and surveillance
subsystems.role: guides aircraft on a precise approach and keeps the pad safe.

subsystems.name: Airspace and traffic management
subsystems.role: sequences arrivals and departures with other aircraft and conventional air traffic.
parts: link to air navigation service provider

subsystems.name: Terminal and cargo handling
subsystems.role: moves people or parcels on and off the aircraft quickly.
parts: lifts or escalators to street level
acoustic enclosure or siting away from homes

subsystems.name: Operations control
subsystems.role: dispatches, monitors and recovers the fleet.

buildSteps.title: Choose and assess the site
buildSteps.detail: Candidates are ranked by wind exposure, obstacle clearance, noise impact on nearby homes, and whether the approach path crosses populated areas.

buildSteps.title: Agree the airspace
buildSteps.detail: An airspace change proposal defines the arrival and departure corridors and how the hub will interact with conventional traffic.

buildSteps.title: Build the structure
buildSteps.detail: A rooftop or ground-level deck is constructed to carry repeated dynamic landing loads, with drainage, fall protection and fire suppression designed for battery fires.

buildSteps.title: Bring in power
buildSteps.detail: A high-voltage supply is installed with a transformer and an on-site battery buffer, because simultaneous fast charging would otherwise spike the local grid.

buildSteps.title: Install navigation and sensors
buildSteps.detail: Beacons, approach lights, wind sensors and surface surveillance are fitted and calibrated against the published approach path.

buildSteps.title: Commission the control systems
buildSteps.detail: The traffic management software is connected to the air navigation service provider and flight-tested with unmanned aircraft first.

buildSteps.title: Certify
buildSteps.detail: Regulators inspect the design, emergency procedures and fire response before passenger operations are permitted.

buildSteps.title: Operate the network
buildSteps.detail: Day-to-day running means rapid turnarounds — landing, passenger or parcel exchange, recharge and departure in a few minutes per aircraft.

prerequisites.why: several types are in flight test; passenger certification is still being completed.
aircraft batteries must recharge in minutes and survive thousands of cycles without losing range.
many aircraft in one small volume of city airspace need automated deconfliction.
regulators in Europe and the United States have published initial design guidance, but it is still evolving.
multiple small rotors and digital flight controls make these aircraft controllable and quiet enough for cities.

pathway.milestone: cargo drone corridors and a small number of purpose-built pads in trials
pathway.unlocks: real data on noise, wind limits and turnaround times.

pathway.milestone: first certified passenger operations on fixed routes between a few hubs
pathway.unlocks: a proven safety and certification template.

pathway.milestone: city networks with a handful of interconnected vertiports linked to rail and transit
pathway.unlocks: journeys that beat road traffic rather than just demonstrate the aircraft.

pathway.milestone: higher-throughput hubs handling continuous rotations with increasing automation
pathway.unlocks: urban air transport that is a routine part of city mobility, if noise and cost allow.
